subject: RE: Parcel question
body:
Good morning,

Thank you for your call last week. I looked up the parcel next to your home on our eligibility map. It is shown in blue, which means three or more units can be built there under current Zoning, and a multifamily project on that parcel could be eligible for streamlining under State law if it met all of the eligibility requirements. Being shown on the map does not mean a project has been proposed, and no applications for this streamlined process have been submitted in your Community Planning Area.  If you would like more detail on the zoning or permit history for that property, the PDS Zoning Counter would be the best place to start.

Also, a reminder that we are still requesting your group's feedback on the Alpine checklist by August 15th, 2024.

Please let me know if you have any other questions.

subject: RE: [External] Building records question
body:

subject: Re: Loveland Trail Improvements Meeting 3/14
body:
Nicholas Brust

Deputy District Director

CA Senator Brian Jones

Good Morning, Mr. Brust,

Thank you for working on this meeting for the trails and other Loveland community priorities, such as fish restocking, reasonable public access hours that server working people and families, and a balance of recreation and wildlife protection in conjunction with water storage policies.

I would like to add that some things are not allowed : 

1}Contractors interested in bidding projects are excluded from steering the proposals.

2)Proposals that push AB 1O2 funds through any brand, for instance, a nonprofit or commercial interest.

One exception might be costs associated with paperwork or title work/  an escrow to incorporate the SDGE easements into public access trails. 

What I would like to suggest:

1) Before the meeting: Clarity from Congressman Issa's office on the legality and restoration of  Forest Service easement-protected hours of Sunrise to Sunset and the encumbrance of the fishing program on Sweetwater's minimum pool. 

2) Invite an SDGE public affairs specialist to discuss the public use of the  Sunrise Powerlink easement roads at Loveland.

3) A neutral subject matter expert contractor on trails, fishing infrastructure,  and other related matters who is in an advisory role only and will not unduly steer or bid on proposals.

4) Participation from a  Regional Waterboards  permitting expert to help define or give feedback on impacts that water regulation standards will or won’t have on our proposals. Confusion on these matters has been stifling in previous meetings.

5) A rubric for choosing proposals created by the Loveland stakeholders in attendance or designed by Mr. Jantz with consideration for feedback from Sweetwater Authority and Loveland advocates/stakeholders.

6) A report back on this meeting at the Alpine Community Planning Group's March 28 meeting.

Please let me know if I can assist you or others in Senator Jones's office with this important meeting. 

Appreciatively,

Russell Walsh

4639 Montiel Truck Trail

subject: Feasibility Study Interview Request - California State Water Resources Control Board
body:
Good afternoon,

My name is Marissa, with Katz & Associates, and I'm part of a team under the California State Water Resources Control Board that is studying the feasibility of consolidating properties with individual groundwater wells or independent water systems east of Alpine with the Padre Dam Municipal Water District.

I'm reaching out today to see if you're interested in participating in an interview that will inform a Feasibility Study.

Background
The California State Water Resources Control Board<https://www.waterboards.ca.gov/> (Board) under the Safe and Affordable Funding for Equity and Resilience (Safer) Drinking Water Program<https://www.waterboards.ca.gov/water_issues/programs/grants_loans/sustainable_water_solutions/safer.html>, is funding planning efforts, including a Feasibility Study (Study), to support communities and help ensure a safe and reliable water supply for the future.

Due to some water quality concerns of existing groundwater wells in the Willowside Terrace community, located just east of the city of Alpine, the Board is conducting a Study to determine if this community can be connected to the Padre Dam Municipal Water District<https://www.padredam.org/> (PDMWD) to ensure a high quality, reliable and sustainable water supply is available for the future.

The Study team is interested in forming an expanded study area to include additional properties near Willowside Terrace that also use an independent water system reliant on groundwater.

As an Alpine resident, the Study team is interested in participating in an interview with you to gather insights into the communities east of Alpine, near the potential study area. The Study team is interested in a range of views, opinions and experiences about independent water systems, the services provided by PDMWD, and the possibility of consolidating independent water systems with the district

Please let me know if you are interested in participating in an interview and what your availability looks like for the next few weeks. Separately, we would like to request time on an upcoming Alpine Community Planning Group agenda for a brief update on the Study.

I look forward to hearing from you.

Marissa Twite (she/her/hers)
Account Supervisor

subject: Report on SANDAG's January 2025 Meetings to the Association of Planning Groups - San Diego County
body:
Good Afternoon APG Members,

Note: The SANDAG Board of Directors held three meetings in the month of
January.

*SANDAG Leadership Changes - New Officers Elected:*
New Chair for SANDAG BOD: Lesa Heebner, City of Solana Beach
New Vice Chair for SANDAG BOD: Joe Lacava, City of San Diego
New Second Vice Chair for SANDAG BOD: John Minto, City of Santee

Jan. 10th - APG comment to Board: Good morning. Congratulations on your
election as the dream team for the officers. I do represent the
unincorporated area, over 500,000 people, and, of course, this seat is not
a voting seat. Today I want to note for the record that the County is not
present and so, therefore; all action taken by this Board today - voting
action - has effectively disenfranchised the Unincorporated Area. We're not
present. And, we don't have a vote. And, I hope in 2025, I expect in 2025,
that this Board will overall do a better job of ensuring that the
Unincorporated Area is not disenfranchised. I realize County being absent
is not the fault of the Board, but there must be something in place that
takes into account that there's over half a million people who are not
participating in the proceedings today. Thank you.

Jan. 31st - APG Comment to the Board: The County of San Diego is not
present. However, the people of the County of San Diego are present.
(Note: County was completely absent for all of the January 2025 BOD
meetings - 10th & 24th & 31st)

*SANDAG CEO, Mario Orso Report:*
-Mario Orso reported that the CFO was adjusting revenue projections on
TransNet funds by a couple of percentage points - between 2 to 4%. This
would be a decrease in expected funding and could affect both MTS and NCTD.
-The Grand Jury report findings and recommendations came as no surprise as
the Office of the Independent Performance Auditor had brought these needed
issues and changes to the Board in their earlier report and they are being
addressed.

*Otay Mesa East and SR 11 Report:*
The Federal agreements with U.S. Customs and Border Protection and with
General Services have set the stage for the beginning of construction and
the relationship SANDAG will have with CBP. Caltrans is also a partner.
If the toll revenues of the Port of Entry are not as projected the
shortfall cannot be made up with TransNet funds.

Ann Fox, Caltrans comment: ...We've done the studies that have shown the
many dollars and jobs lost and the air pollution created by the long delays
along our shared borders. California has invested more than half of the
$1.3 billion project cost and has spent hundreds of millions more building
out the corridor and the connections we have with State Routes 905 and 125.
...We have built the infrastructure, the new roads, the utilities, the
technology, the air quality monitors out there, in addition to over 180
acres of environmental mitigation.

Jack Fisher, City of Imperial Beach comment: (reading Brian Bilbray letter)
"... I'm sure some other members will not continue to support the expansion
of the economic growth with the environmental damage without addressing
historical and future environmental and public health threats caused by
such economic development. I ask that every board member here question if
their city council or county board would vote for any project knowing its
environmental and health problems if it was going to be anywhere close to
the disastrous situation that citizens of the South Bay faced everyday?"
I can't tell you how frustrated I am because I know with the increased
traffic and commerce Mexico will continue to grow. Their population will
continue to grow. It was mentioned that just this operation port of entry
opening will create 90,000 jobs on the U.S. side. I would imagine that
number probably doubles or triples on the Mexico side. Still without the
infrastructure.

*TransNet Major Corridor Projects Update: State Route 67:*
Sam Amen, Karina Cantera-Angel & Tracy D'Aoust Roberts of Caltrans -
presented 3 alternatives for the improvement of SR 67 understanding that
evacuation was the highest consideration. Project area is SR 67 from
Highland Valley in Ramona to Mapleview in Lakeside. Alternative #1 provides
4 outbound lanes and one inbound lane dedicated to inbound emergency
vehicles. Alternatives #2 & #3 provide some of these benefits, but not
consistently throughout the project area and include the use of shoulders
as "lanes" in an emergency.

APG comment to Board: The Unincorporated Area has been partnering with
Caltrans and we thank Sam, Karina, Tracy, Melina, Stephen and Tyler for
their dedication. Safety is always first.  Caltrans states, "The primary
goal of the SR 67 Highway Improvements Project is to increase capacity
during emergencies to significantly reduce evacuation times."  Safety is
always first. SANDAG serves over 3.3 million people across the region;
however, some benefit more than others. Had SANDAG delivered on the
promises of TransNet to the Unincorporated Area - Measure G would have
passed. The experience of those patiently awaiting their turn at the
Regional funding bucket has been disheartening. 1988 and 2004 turned into a
resounding "no" in 2024 for rural communities on Measure G. The LA fires
demonstrate a clear and present danger to rural highway travelers -
evacuees may live locally or may be visiting from the city. Caltrans has
stood ready and willing to deliver highway safety. Alternative #1 delivers
on the Promise. Let us immediately put into place emergency widening to
move evacuees through the current SR 67 gauntlet of bottlenecks. Safety is
always first. SANDAG does not want to be the obstacle to improvements
necessary to avoid the catastrophic results of the LA fires. The elected
Board members would not want the public to rightfully be able to say that
they could have done more to prevent a loss of life and property. Thank you.

Steve Vaus, City of Poway; Carolina Chavez, City of Chula Vista; Rebecca
Jones, City of San Marcos; Kevin Shin, City of Carlsbad; Bill Wells, City
of El Cajon; John Minto, City of Santee;  & Terry Gaasterland, City of Del
Mar all made comments: All of these city representatives were positive in
their comments emphasizing the need to expand SR 67 for evacuation purposes
and Mayors Minto, Jones, Wells and Gaasterland specifically endorsed the
selection of Alternative #1. There were no comments opposing Caltrans
proposed solutions to SR 67. The Board of Directors was supportive.

Lesa Heebner, City of Solana Beach & SANDAG Chair comment:  "What can we do
now?"

Allan Kosup, Caltrans response: We have an emergency widening project that
just began this week on SR 67. The environmental report was received last
week and the project was begun immediately. It will be over the next six
months. This will provide more space in the event of an evacuation.

*APG News:*
-Thank you to all who were able to attend our in-person APG meeting held on
Saturday, January 4th, 2025. A quorum was established and voting actions
were taken.

*APG Officers elected for 2025 (one year terms):*
Chair, Robin Joy Maxson
Vice Chair, Eileen Delaney
Secretary, Carol Hake

*APG Representative to SANDAG Board of Directors (two year terms):*
Primary Representative, Robin Joy Maxson
Alternate Representative, Eileen Delaney

*APG Representatives to SANDAG Policy Advisory Committees:*

Regional Planning Committee:
APG Representative: Ron Nehring
APG Alternate: Kiki Skagen Munshi

Transportation Committee:
APG Representative: Jim Custeau
APG Alternate: Paul Dombkowski

Borders Committee:
APG Representative: Lynne Malinowski
APG Alternate: Harriet Taylor

Public Safety Committee:
APG Representative: Paul Dombkowski
APG Alternate: Eileen Delaney

Audit Committee:
APG Representative: Carol Hake

-Update: Congressman Darrell Issa - representing the majority of the
unincorporated area in San Diego County - has not set a meeting date with
the APG as of this report. Since July, the APG has been working to set up a
joint meeting with the Congressman, SANDAG CEO Mario Orso and our APG
members without success. SANDAG CEO Mario Orso has stated he will be
available and happy to attend our joint meeting. Congressman Issa has not
been available and very little communication has come from his office. The
APG sent a request to his Chief of Staff, Veronica Smith Wong. She has
responded, but not with a set date, yet.

The subject of the meeting will be:
"Transportation funding and safety in the Unincorporated Area; addressing
fatality rate on rural highways, safe wildfire evacuation, lack of public
transportation resulting in geographic isolation of vulnerable populations
and continued diversion of transportation funds from rural highway
projects."

Several Planning/Sponsor Groups have already sent letters to Congressman
Issa. Thank you Travis and the Alpine CPG for sending us a copy of yours.
If any group wishes to contact Issa directly, email his Chief of
Staff Veronica Smith Wong: veronica.smith@mail.house.gov

*Questions from APG members*
No questions received this month.

*Links*
SANDAG BOD and PAC meetings for calendar 2025:
https://legistarweb-production.s3.amazonaws.com/uploads/attachment/pdf/3108009/Item_3_-_Revised_2025_Legislative_Calendar.pdf

Original SANDAG documents and meeting minutes are available directly from
SANDAG's Board of Directors website:
https://www.sandag.org/meetings-and-events/board-of-directors

Robin Joy Maxson, Representative to SANDAG
Association of Planning Groups - San Diego County

subject: ACPG Loveland Letter's of Support; Sunrise to Sunset & SDGE Access Road Use.
body:
Travis LyonChair Alpine Community Planning Group

Good Morning, Travis,

I am requesting copies of the letters of support we recently discussed that were  put before the ACPG board for a successful vote. 

Some Loveland advocates and recreation users have asked me to follow up on these letters of support. Travis, I urgently need you to forward the letters of support to me. These are crucial for our advocacy efforts, especially in light of the support we have garnered from many other community leaders. Please send me, "reply all"  the letters of support for restoring sunrise to sunset and using the maintenance roads in the SDGE Powerlink easement area.

You might benefit from some follow-up I can provide regarding your recent agenda item for Loveland trails proposals: 

Last night, Sweetwater's BOD passed a motion that the 5 Loveland trails proposal items you reviewed will make up the work plan management will send to the California funding and work oversight group, the Department of Water Resources (DWR). Please see the image below for a rough version of the site plan. 

Travis, your continued involvement and the momentum we (the community) have created, including the commitment of  $75,000 for the master plan, are crucial for the success of the Loveland project. Your efforts will serve our communities on recreation and help defend Loveland wildlife and our lake user neighbors and friends in the face of potential bad ideas and acts against them by the Sweetwater Authority. We have seen the impact of such disasters in the past year, and your support and that of the ACPG is invaluable. 

Best regards,

Russell

> travislyonacpg@gmail.com>, Cherry Diefenbach <csdiefenbach@sbcglobal.net>,
> Sandra Farrell, <tovcsg.chair@gmail.com>, Rebecca Falk <rebfalk7@gmail.com>,
> <petersonenv@hotmail.com>, Jennifer Haider <jennehaider@gmail.com>
>
>
> *SANDAG Board Actions and Discussions - March 2023*
>
> *SANDAG Retreat 2023:*
> March 10th meeting - a Board Retreat held at the Salt Drift Pointe, 536
> 13th Street, Imperial Beach from 8:30 to 3:30. Both the APG Representative
> (Robin Maxson) and Alternate (Eileen Delaney) attended and participated in
> the team building activities. The goal of the Retreat was to build a
> regional planning mindset for the Board members and to develop a set of
> criteria/traits for the next SANDAG CEO. Recruiting and interviewing has
> narrowed the candidate field to six individuals.
>
> *Caltrans:*
> Roy Abboud and Mario Orso - communicated to the APG Rep that Caltrans had
> 2.6 billion in funding for the unincorporated area projects. Also, that
> they would be "speeding up" projects on the SR 67.
>
> *125 Toll Road Action Plan:*
> March 24th Meeting - Coleen Clementson reported that SANDAG had signed the
> contract with the group (unnamed) that would be running the new back-office
> system and that it would be up and running by the end of the year.
> Independent Performance Auditor - Courtney Ruby will be presenting the
> results of the audit at the next Board meeting. (As it turned out a Special
> SANDAG Board meeting was called for March 31st to specifically discuss the
> results of this internal audit.)
> Report on options discussed with South Bay leaders for early pay off of
> 125 Toll Road would be brought forth in a future meeting.
>
> March 31 Special Board Meeting - The report from the Office of the
> Independent Performance Auditor released a report on March 27th resulted in
> a Special meeting of the Board to be called.  This report was previously
> sent to APG members in a separate email, but here is the link:
> https://www.sandag.org/-/media/SANDAG/Documents/PDF/about/office-of-the-independent-performance-auditor/reports-and-documents/sr-125-investigation-report-final.pdf
>
> The report revealed ongoing, egregious lack of oversight and a pattern of
> failure to take action to correct a multitude of issues with operation of
> the 125 Toll Road.
> Board members questioned every aspect contributing to this situation:
> Why wasn't the Board informed of the back-office discrepancies in tolls
> collected and toll user accounts?
> Why have we signed a contract with the same company that did not deliver
> on the contractual requirements?
> Why would we contract again with companies that did not collect nor record
> tolls correctly?
> What is the criteria for selecting a company for the contract?
> Why wasn't it reported to the Board that tolls stopped being collected due
> to equipment disconnect sooner?
> Why is SANDAG using QuickBooks for accounting purposes?
> Who in SANDAG's executive leadership knew of these issues and when?
> What is SANDAG's Whistle Blower policy?
> Why did SANDAG allow a culture of intimidation to exist with respect to
> the former CEO?
> Why were financial reports repeatedly corrected and the issues leading to
> faulty numbers not corrected instead?
> How much money has the contractor been paid for the 125 Toll Road and for
> other projects they manage, for example the I-15 managed lanes.
> How can we ensure that the same accounting issues have not occurred with
> the I-15?
> How much money in tolls was lost overall?
>
> Board member comments were:
> "After I pick up my jaw from the floor I have a few questions."
> "This isn't just a black eye for SANDAG, but two black eyes."
> "We need to investigate potential fraud."
> "We need to rebuild trust in SANDAG."
>
> The Independent Performance Auditor's recommendations were accepted by the
> Board and more Board actions and answers to questions and concerns would be
> forthcoming at the April 14th regular Board meeting.
>
> *Report of SANDAG's Draft Fiscal Year 2024 Budget Program - Capital
> Projects:*
> SANDAG reported on the DRAFT FY 2024 Budget. The presentation included the
> project and funding allocation of both TransNet and non-TransNet funded
> projects. The hand out (see attachment) was a visual overview of the
> projects and location - Note the lack of projects planned (funded) in the
> unincorporated area of the County. Based on this discrepancy in funding for
> the unincorporated area and for areas of North County the Board heard many
> complaints from its own members.
>
> APG comment to Board: "Good morning. Thank you. Representing the
> unincorporated area where we're 500 thousand strong. I understand that we
> use the limited funds where it can do the most good. But I would like to
> remind everyone to keep in mind that we do have a large population outside
> of the populated corridor. And, that in addition to the 500 thousand, we do
> have thousands of visitors on the weekends. So, I see a lot of funding for
> bikeways which is good for health and greenhouse gas reduction. But I see
> very limited funding for our Vision Zero Plan to reduce highway severe
> injuries and fatalities. I don't see a lot of money in the unincorporated
> area where all of the visitors are coming on the weekends and where there
> is a tremendous amount of pressure on those roadways. Also, I don't see
> that a priority is being given to wildfire evacuation. And, with two
> unsuccessful wildfire evacuations in '03 and '07 it is not a matter of if;
> but when we will have another one. Right now it is green, but it won't be
> that situation in June. I would like to know how SANDAG determines the
> funding allocation - how do they decide that balance between a population
> that is concentrated and a population that is spread out? Yet there is
> still a need in both areas. And, I do appreciate all of your work, but I
> want to understand how that calculus is made. Thank you."
>
> Susan Huntington (SANDAG staff) response: The annual budget really looks
> toward the Regional Plan prioritization process. So the Regional Plan is
> our long term plan and it establishes the implementation schedule of the
> projects. We use multiple different criterias in that project
> prioritization process. The annual budget looks at when those projects are
> meant to be open; like if a project is meant to be open in 2035 we need to
> get started on that project in say 2025. So, we're really looking to
> implement the Regional Plan as we pull the budget together. And, all of
> those criteria for prioritization come through the Regional Plan process."
>
> You can also view my comment at the meeting link:
> https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=arKeg7IFk7w   02:06:30
> and here is the link to the budget document:
> https://www.sandag.org/-/media/SANDAG/Documents/PDF/funding/budget/sandag-program-budget-fy-2024.pdf#page=6
>
> *SANDAG's Regional Housing Needs Allocation (RHNA):*
> Report on RHNA from Sacramento's Housing and Community Development (HCD)
> staff Megan Kirkeby and Marisa Prasse.
> The HCD reported that future development continued to be focused on
> population corridors and not near open spaces or places without
> transportation options. This effectively eliminates rural and semi-rural
> areas for housing.
> Board discussion on the increased legislation from Sacramento (SB 35 and
> SB 423) that punished/fined cities for not meeting their RHNA numbers.
> Cities reported that Sacramento was applying a state-wide housing solution
> to individual cities instead of allowing a more reasonable and attainable
> allocation to be made regionally as some communities had more buildable
> land available than others.  Some unincorporated communities are located
> near job centers and should not be dismissed as potential housing locations
> due to a lack of public transit options.
>
> *APG Update:*
> In addition to this SANDAG report the APG has received acceptance of our
> Associate membership (non-voting) invitation to Community Sponsor Groups by
> Bonsall (Jennifer Haider), Jacumba (Cherry Diefenbach) and Twin Oaks Valley
> (Joseph Bunn). We will formally accept their membership at our June 3rd APG
> meeting. Welcome to Bonsall, Jacumba and Twin Oaks Valley!
>
> Report Submitted by:
> Robin Joy Maxson, Representative to SANDAG
> Association of Planning Groups - San Diego County
>

 Mr. Walsh,
The planning group took 2 actions at last month's meeting related to Loveland Reservoir.
   - We voted to support the 5 projects proposed by Sweetwater Authority to be funded by the $750,000 in funds awarded by the State of California.  

   - We voted to authorize the chair to draft letters of support for Sunrise to Sunset for trail users at Loveland Reservoir.

Tonight the group will vote to approve the two above items as part of the approval of the meeting minutes.  I am still drafting letters of support for Sunrise to Sunset and they have not yet been sent out.
The planning group discussed taking an official position on expanded trail use on SDGE easements, but did not take action on that proposal.
There are no items on tonight's agenda related to Loveland Reservoir.  I too have a family and am currently addressing a medical emergency.  I am not sure if I will be at the meeting tonight, but I wanted to provide you with this update before you made the trip to the meeting.
I expect to send out letters of support for sunrise to sunset very soon.  I appreciate all your efforts to support Loveland Reservoir trail users.

workshop for members of the Planning Group regarding the role that planning

subject: Re: Sunrise to Sunset Discussion at Alpine Community Planning Group.
body:
Steve HalesDirector Friends of Loveland Reservoir

Hello Steve,

Steve, I want to express my sincere gratitude to you and your board for the commendable actions you've taken in support of Sunrise to Sunset. Your efforts have not gone unnoticed and are greatly appreciated. 

Have you reached out to Congressman Issa? Our easement is primarily a federal issue, and while we need follow-through, and community support everywhere we can get it, Congressman Issa is our strongest ally where the Forest Service is concerned. Please ask your board to promote a quality petition for progress on the restoration of  Sunrise to Sunset access ASAP.  As you said recently, agencies like to work with and respond to groups like Friends of Loveland Reservoir. If you need help, please let me and others know, perhaps via membership and a website.  

Your help at the ACPG is important:The ACPG has been a good base at times for Loveland Advocacy but there have been let downs too. Your board members know that  I went to a half dozen meetings with the Alpine Community Planning group for help with Loveland in the year before it was drained and to many meetings since. In the spring of 2022 a strong vote passed by ACPG to encourage Sweetwater to come to the Alpine Group. There was a least one previous resolution to write letters of support on recreation themes.  However, the chair did not complete these tasks despite the strong votes. The same thing appears to be happening with April's nearly unanimous vote for a letter of support from the ACPG on the Sunrise to Sunset. I believe you are aware through CC'd email on this trajectory. We need to work together so the ACPG honors community work and interests at Loveland and the work of the people on the planning advisory board itself on behalf of Loveland Reservoir so we can have success on Sunrise to Sunset and full defense of future complete dewatering which are here. We all agree that land use organizations are falling short of legal easement adherence and should be advised and strenuously petitioned to do otherwise. 

Please check your emails from me about Sweetwater's goal to float 200 acres of solar panels at Sweetwater Reservoir. 

The minimum water levels to float that industrial-type project will likely come from Loveland Reservoir and create new cyclical dewatering episodes. Sweetwater refuses to remove the threat, which is a factor. The good news is that it is being challenged locally in South Bay and here by us. 

Appreciatively,

Russell

Russell Walsh

4639 Montiel Truck Trail

Jamul CA, 91935

Hi Russell,

  

FOLR supports honoring the easement terms including sunrise to sunset.  We press for it when we meet with the Forrest Service or with the Sweet Water Authority.  While some progress is being made on many issues, we have had about as much success as you have in getting them to honor that commitment.

  

I’ll bring up the ACPG letter at the next FOLR board meeting.  Of course you can also contact the ACPG directly and ask yourself. 

  

Steve

Subject: Re: Sunrise to Sunset Discussion at Alpine Communiity Planning Group.

  

Steve Hales

Director Friends of Loveland

CC Karen Wood Executive Director Friends of Loveland

  

  

Steve,

  

I am following up on your letter from April regarding FOLR support for Sunrise to Sunset at Loveland Reservoir.

As we near the point of longest day length in the summer of 2023 I am curious as to progress made, or effort given for our nature viewer and other recreation users on this matter. 

  

Also, I have advised you about how Sweetwater Authority is a constant applicant and recipient of State and Federal grants, yet is comfortable shortchanging taxpayers and citizens on even the limited sunrise to sunset access to Loveland's shoreline. You told me that FOLR supports that. How can we work together to challenge this taxpayer inequity so that FOLR followers and all other lake users may experience the therapeutic recreation and sometimes food aquistion rights they own at  Loveland Reservoir.

  

Thank you for you work for  nature lovers , fishers and hikers who need this recreation and proper voice and action in our communities by our leaders. I have letters of support on Sunrise to Sunset from Supervisor Anderson if you can use that in you advocacy. The ACPG was almost unaniously in favor of a letter of support to Sweetwater and the Forest Service on Sunrise to Sunset a few months ago, with the FOLR member being the only one to abstain. However , it appears the Chair has not notified or responded to concerns about the creation and issue of that letter. Please follow up on that with Chair Travis Lyon. 

  

Russell Walsh

  

4639 Montiel Truck Trail

Jamul CA, 91935

619-922-6235

  

On Friday, April 14, 2023 at 03:33:03 PM PDT, Steve Hales <steve@hales.xyz> wrote:

  

  

Russell,

 

The FOLR board supports sunrise to sunset hours at Loveland.

 

You are incorrect about what happened at the ACPG meeting.  In Darlene’s position as a member of the ACPG board, she abstained from voting on the motion – but she did not vote “No” or try to “block” it as you say.  And she abstained only after it was obvious the motion would pass anyway.

 

Regardless, Darlene can vote however she likes as a member of the ACPG board, without FOLR approving or justifying that vote. 

 

I hope this clarifies the misunderstanding.

 

Steve

FOLR

Subject: Sunrise to Sunset Discussion at Alpine Communiity Planning Group.

 

 

 

Karen Wood

Executive Director 

Friends of Loveland Reservoir

Alpine CA

 

Hello  Karen,

 

Thank you for your recent complimentary work on the Loveland fishing float platform and other items of concern for Loveland Lake users. 

 

During the Alpine community planning group meeting last week, a significant issue regarding access to Loveland Reservoir was raised. Your board member, Darlene Cossio,  who is also on the planning group board, attempted to block the group's motion for a letter of support  to Sweetwater Authority and the US Forest Service for sunrise-to-sunset access. She claimed that the issue was already being addressed.

 

Would you please clarify what your board members' actions and comments mean for restoring access at Loveland according to the easement? Why does your board member see this being resolved so that she would block a letter of support and make the statements I am asking about?

 

Another spring and summer of afternoon and early evening recreation at Loveland is slipping away from working people and their families. Please support independent advocates in requesting that the ACPG bring the Cleveland National Forest administrators back to the ACPG meeting for a public follow-up on our meeting with them at the ACPG  last October. 

 

Appreciatively,

 

Russell

subject: Feasibility Study Interview Request - California State Water Resources Control Board
body:
Good afternoon,

My name is Marissa, with Katz & Associates, and I'm part of a team under the California State Water Resources Control Board that is studying the feasibility of consolidating properties with individual groundwater wells or independent water systems east of Alpine with the Padre Dam Municipal Water District.

I'm reaching out today to see if your group is interested in participating in an interview that will inform a Feasibility Study.

Background
The California State Water Resources Control Board<https://www.waterboards.ca.gov/> (Board) under the Safe and Affordable Funding for Equity and Resilience (Safer) Drinking Water Program<https://www.waterboards.ca.gov/water_issues/programs/grants_loans/sustainable_water_solutions/safer.html>, is funding planning efforts, including a Feasibility Study (Study), to support communities and help ensure a safe and reliable water supply for the future.

Due to some water quality concerns of existing groundwater wells in the Willowside Terrace community, located just east of the city of Alpine, the Board is conducting a Study to determine if this community can be connected to the Padre Dam Municipal Water District<https://www.padredam.org/> (PDMWD) to ensure a high quality, reliable and sustainable water supply is available for the future.

The Study team is interested in forming an expanded study area to include additional properties near Willowside Terrace that also use an independent water system reliant on groundwater.

As planning groups serving the communities east of Alpine, the Study team is interested in participating in an interview with you to gather insights into the communities near the potential study area. The Study team is interested in a range of views, opinions and experiences about independent water systems, the services provided by PDMWD, and the possibility of consolidating independent water systems with the district

Please let me know if you are interested in participating in an interview and what your availability looks like for the next few weeks.

I look forward to hearing from you.

Marissa Twite (she/her/hers)
Account Supervisor

subject: FW: Park Fee Changes Starting February 18, 2025
body:
Greg,

FYI - see below.

Carl McCullough
Region Manager, I-8 Corridor
County of San Diego Parks and Recreation Department
Office: (858) 966-1357
Cell: (619) 961-0159

From: McCullough, Carl <Carl.McCullough@sdcounty.ca.gov>
Sent: Tuesday, February 4, 2025 11:44 AM
To: pinevalleyplanninggroup@gmail.com
Subject: Park Fee Changes Starting February 18, 2025

Hi,

At the County of San Diego Parks and Recreation Department, we take great pride in maintaining beautiful, safe, and accessible outdoor spaces for everyone to enjoy. To continue providing high-quality parks, trails, and recreation services, we will be making some adjustments to our park service fees starting February 18, 2025.
This is our first fee update in nearly 11 years, and while we’ve worked hard to keep costs as low as possible, this change is necessary to help offset rising maintenance and operating expenses. The updates also align our fees with similar parks and facilities in the region while ensuring that we continue to deliver best-in-nation outdoor experiences.

What’s Changing?
Most of the fee increases are just a few dollars, but they will help us keep our parks safe, clean, and well-maintained for generations to come. Here are a few examples of the adjustments:

  *   Day Use Parking: Increasing from $3.00 to $5.00 per day
  *   RV Partial Hook-Up Campsite: Increasing from $29 to $35 per night
  *   Camping Reservations: Now include up to two pets and one extra vehicle at no additional cost
  *   Other small increases apply to rentals, permits, and additional park services

To see the full list of updated fees, please visit our 2025_DPR_User_Fee_Changes_01.17.25.pdf<https://www.sdparks.org/content/dam/sdparks/en/pdf/public-meetings/fee_increase/2025_DPR_User_Fee_Changes_01.17.25.pdf>. For more information on why these changes are happening, check out our FAQs_Park User Fee Increase 01.17.25.pdf<https://www.sdparks.org/content/dam/sdparks/en/pdf/public-meetings/fee_increase/FAQs_Park%20User%20Fee%20Increase%2001.17.25.pdf>.

Why Are Fees Increasing?
The cost of maintaining our 158 parks, 389 miles of trails, and over 58,000 acres of land has risen significantly over the past decade. Adjusting our fees will allow us to:
✔ Continue offering high-quality park experiences and amenities
✔ Keep trails, facilities, and green spaces safe and well-maintained
✔ Expand and improve park programs and services for all ages and abilities
Even with these updates, our park fees remain affordable and continue to offer exceptional value compared to similar park systems.

Ensuring Parks Remain Accessible for Everyone
We believe that everyone should have access to nature—which is why we continue to offer financial assistance programs and free or low-cost activities:
🌿 Discounted Programs: Veterans, seniors, and groups may qualify for discounts on fees and reservations.
🏕 First-Time Camping Program: A free initiative designed to introduce new campers to the joys of the outdoors.
🎉 Low-Cost or Free Activities: Most of our recreation programs and events are available at reduced or no cost.
We are committed to making the outdoors accessible and enjoyable for all members of our community.

Thank You for Your Support!
We appreciate your understanding and continued support as we make these necessary updates. Your visits, participation, and enthusiasm help keep our parks vibrant and welcoming for everyone.
If you have any questions or would like more details, please visit our Fees Increase Feb. 18<https://www.sdparks.org/content/sdparks/en/news-events/news-stories/Fees-Increase-Feb-18.html>.

We look forward to seeing you at the parks!

Thanks & Go Aztecs,

Carl McCullough

subject: RE: Objective Design Standards (ODS) Checklist - Alpine
body:
Good morning,

Thank you for your continued coordination with our Objective Design Standards (ODS) project. As discussed, State laws that are already in effect require that any housing developments eligible for streamlining approval be reviewed with clear, objective standards regarding design aspects such as materials, colors, etc. Typically, these would be projects that include affordable housing units.  Design standards that are not objective cannot be applied to these projects.

To ensure we have objective design standards available for any potential applications, our team used your existing Design Review Checklist as a template to create an Objective Design Review Checklist that clarifies any subjective language and maintains the visual integrity of housing developments in your community. We kindly request your group send any feedback on the checklist by August 15th, 2024.

The Objective Design Review Checklist will serve as a supplemental form for projects eligible for streamlined approval under state law. It will not replace the current Design Review Checklist<https://www.sandiegocounty.gov/content/dam/sdc/pds/drb/AlpineDesignReviewChecklistFINAL1.pdf>, which will continue to apply to projects not eligible for the streamlined review. While no applications for this streamlined process have been submitted in your Community Planning Area, the Objective Design Review Checklist will be applicable if one is received. We are finalizing this Objective Design Review Checklist and will make it easily accessible online for potential applications eligible for these State laws.

Attached is the draft Objective Design Review version of your community’s existing Design Review Checklist, and a map delineating potentially eligible areas for this streamlined process. A strikethrough indicates a proposed removal of language, while an underline indicates a proposed change/addition.  Also attached is a PDF version for your reference. There may also be highlighted language or comment bubbles that we are requesting specific feedback on, regarding unclear language or unclear measurements.  There are additional details in the original e-mail below.

We will work to incorporate your suggestions into the checklist which will be accessible on our website in Fall 2024. While there is some flexibility to make changes in the future, staff availability and allocation may make it challenging to respond urgently to suggestions for edits after that date. Therefore, please ensure you submit any requests for modifications by August 15th, 2024, so your feedback can be incorporated into the checklist before it is made available online.

Please let us know if you have any questions as you review the document. We appreciate your continued collaboration and commitment to enhancing our unincorporated communities.

[cid:image001.png@01DA7ABA.EF015A80]<http://www.sdcpds.org/>
Luis Duran
Planner III | Planning & Development Services | Long Range Planning
County of San Diego | 5510 Overland Ave. Suite 310 | San Diego, CA 92123|
• (619) 214-4698  |  • Luis.Duran@sdcounty.ca.gov<mailto:Luis.Duran@sdcounty.ca.gov>

From: Duran, Luis
Sent: Friday, March 22, 2024 4:03 PM
To: cdean@benderdean.com
Subject: Objective Design Standards (ODS) Checklist - Alpine

Hello Mr. Dean,

I hope this email finds you well. Following our recent presentation at your Design Review Board (DRB) meeting on February 22, 2024. I am pleased to update you on the latest progress regarding the Objective Design Standards (ODS) project.

To recap, our presentation centered around State laws which allow for a streamlined process for eligible multifamily projects, and how design standards can be implemented in that process. Eligible projects need to meet all eligibility requirements and objective design standards at the time of application, or their development cannot be streamlined through a ministerial process. Our project team is working to edit your existing Design Review Checklist to clarify any subjective language to maintain the visual integrity of your community in the case an eligible project application is submitted. Attached is a draft “Objective” version of the Alpine Checklist with a corresponding map, delineating potentially eligible areas for streamlined housing development.

A few notes as you review the attached documents:

MAP: State law states that a multifamily development “contains two or more residential units”.  According to the California Department of Housing and Community Development, a new single-family development and an attached accessory dwelling unit when built together are considered multifamily and are eligible for streamlining under SB 35.  An applicant would still need to meet all eligibility requirements to streamline their project. These eligible parcels are distinguished by a pink color.  The blue parcels are eligible for streamlining under State law, where three or more units can be built under current Zoning. The attached maps have been updated to reflect recent State laws in effect as of March 2024.

CHECKLIST: Attached is a Microsoft Word document containing tracked changes.  A strikethrough indicates a proposed removal of language, while an underline indicates proposed change/addition.  Also attached is a PDF version for your reference. The Design Review Checklist for your community may include goals or intentions related to your original Design Guidelines. As this draft is for ease of use, we have removed these to strictly focus on the design standards that must be followed. This makes the checklist shorter and easier to read. There may also be highlighted language or comment bubbles that we are requesting specific feedback on, regarding unclear language or unclear measurements.

As discussed previously, this project will not be updating or changing Alpine’s Form Based Code (FBC).  The Draft Objective Design Standards Checklist attached is for the areas not covered by the FBC.  We kindly request your group review the attached Checklist to ensure that it accurately reflects the intent of your existing community’s design standards. Please submit your initial feedback no later than April 23rd, 2024.

We appreciate your collaboration and commitment to enhancing our unincorporated communities.

For further information on ODS, please visit the following links: Objective Design Standards | Engage San Diego County<https://engage.sandiegocounty.gov/ods> and Objective Design Standards (sandiegocounty.gov)<https://www.sandiegocounty.gov/content/sdc/pds/longrangeplanning/ods/>

subject: Fw: Loveland Community  Powerpoint. and Thoughts.
body:
Hi Robin, 
I may stop by APG next month to give a Loveland update in the public comments.If you would like to talk before then please let me know.  You can see from the CC'd email. I wanted to own this for a while  to make it big(ger). Let's see what happens. 
Let's get sunrise to sunset especially. The only reason we don't have it is because the Forest Service giving it back betrays their betrayal over the last 4 years,.and maybe  highlights something like civil rights violations.

Russell 
   ----- Forwarded Message ----- From: Russell Walsh <russellwalsh2003@yahoo.com>To: Nicholas Brust <nicholas.brust@sen.ca.gov>Cc: Andrew Hayes <andrew.hayes@sen.ca.gov>; barryjantz@gmail.com <barryjantz@gmail.com>; Brian Jones <brian.jones@sen.ca.gov>Sent: Friday, March 15, 2024 at 09:16:05 AM PDTSubject: Loveland Community Powerpoint. and Thoughts.
 Hi Nick,
Here is the community  Powerpoint.
It's not exactly what Andrew Hayes asked me for last year.   He wanted a concensus on what to do with the 750k,  but I thought our loses at Loveland merited getting more community input and selling some bigger enthusiasm for projects than the 750k and I hope that does work out. There seems to be interest. 

Thanks for being there with us these last months and last night. 
I felt like you walked back on the SDGE  thing compared to our phone call, but will assume you are being careful not to get yourself, or Senator Jones blamed for setbacks in this possibly complicated scheme. It might not be that complicated, Either way,  please continue to put good intentions into the easement use and the alternatives that will get people using those hard to reach areas. Please update me on SDGE easement progress through CPUC or wherever it needs to go. 
This  is turning into a bit of a  circus and I am a fighter not a clown.  Sort of kidding, It will  be a big good circus with many  a positve outcomes. Please get lots of people on golden shovels that they earned at the end.
I will stick around the 750K scene to present the community  power point when that's part of it, I owe that to people.  Hopefully, I can help stop a few stupid things from happening like letting Sweetwater con us into letting the fishing float go.

The other things. matter, fish stocking, sunrise to sunset,  and I will assume the same idea as above, you are not in a postition to make promises about them but you are on it as you said. I will probably continue to  be too, fighting.
It was nice to meet you,
Thanks again,
Russell

> To:
> Cc: Clerk of the Board <clerkoftheboard@sandag.org>
>
>
> Dear Members of the Board,
>
> As mentioned at the Board of Directors meeting last Friday, I wanted to
> provide an update on two pieces of legislation recently introduced in the
> state legislature that, if enacted, would modify the composition of the
> SANDAG Board of Directors:
>
> *AB 24 (DeMaio)*
> This bill, introduced by Assemblymember Carl DeMaio, proposes modifying
> the SANDAG Board of Directors by removing one of the two County Board of
> Supervisors seats and replacing it with a representative from the San Diego
> County Association of Planning Groups. It would also require the remaining
> County Board representative to be from an unincorporated area of the
> county. The bill has been double-referred to the Assembly Local Government
> Committee and the Assembly Transportation Committee. It currently does not
> have a scheduled hearing date.
>
> *SB 240 (Jones)*
> This bill, introduced by Senate Minority Leader Brian Jones, proposes to
> replace the secondary representative from the County Board of Supervisors
> with a resident from an unincorporated area of the County, as selected by a
> majority of the county’s community planning groups, to serve a 1-year term.
> The bill also eliminates the requirement that one Board of Supervisors
> member be from a substantially incorporated district and the other from an
> unincorporated district. This bill has not yet been referred to a policy
> committee in the Senate.
>
> We will continue to monitor these bills and provide you with updates
> accordingly.
>
> Thank you,
> Mario
>

My name is Michelle Torby, and I am an intern with the Institute for Public
Strategies (IPS). IPS is a non-profit organization that focuses on the
prevention of binge and underage drinking in San Diego County.

Our organization would like to present at the Valle de Oro Community
Planning Group monthly meeting. We would like to do a 15-20 minute capacity building
workshop for members of the Planning Group regarding the role that planning
groups have in preventing excessive alcohol outlet density which
contributes to binge and underage drinking.

Thank you for your consideration, and I look forward to hearing from you.

Best regards,

Michelle Torby

body:
PRIVILEGED AND CONFIDENTIAL
ATTORNEY-CLIENT COMMUNICATION

Travis,

Hani forwarded this to me too. Answers to your two questions:

1. April 4 is not your regular meeting date so it has to be noticed as a special meeting. The agenda has to be posted at least 24 hours ahead and sent to each member, and the group can only act on what is on that agenda. If you want to cover everything that was on the 3/28 agenda, list all of it. I would leave the Modus item off if they aren't ready.

2. Yes. Policy I-1 asks for the group's recommendation, it does not require the applicant to present first. This has already been continued twice at their request. If they aren't ready for the April 25 meeting you can put it on the agenda anyway and let the group decide whether to act or continue it. Keep in mind this is a wireless facility and the County is subject to the federal shot clock, so PDS won't hold its review waiting on the group. If no recommendation comes in the staff report will say so.

Please don't forward this to the applicant.

Laura

PRIVILEGED & CONFIDENTIAL
ATTORNEY-CLIENT COMMUNICATION / ATTORNEY WORK PRODUCT

Travis,

My advice:

- You don't need to confirm anything for Mr. Walsh about what Sweetwater did or didn't receive. That is between him and Sweetwater.
- The group acts by vote at a noticed meeting. Any letter of support that went out on behalf of the ACPG should reflect an action the group took, and the same goes for withdrawing one. You should not retract, amend or confirm a letter on your own, and you should not contact the Sheriff's station about it on the group's behalf.
- If you or other members think the group needs to revisit the letters, put it on the December 5 agenda as an action item and let the group decide.
- If he wants copies of the letters or the minutes where they were approved, refer him to PDS so it goes through the County's public records process.
- Keep any reply short, something like "Thank you, any further action on this item will be taken up by the group at a noticed meeting." Don't get into the merits.

Let me know if you want to talk before the meeting.

Marcus

To: Travis Lyon <travislyonacpg@gmail.com>

PRIVILEGED AND CONFIDENTIAL
ATTORNEY-CLIENT COMMUNICATION
Travis,
Under the Brown Act a member can only participate from a remote location if that location is listed on the posted agenda, the agenda is posted there, and the public can get in. The other option (AB 2449) requires audio and video, a quorum in the room, and is limited in how often a member can use it. The group isn't set up for that, so my advice is no one participates by phone or Zoom. A member who isn't physically there doesn't count toward the quorum and can't vote.

subject: SANDAG Vision Zero
body:
Hello All,

Last week I met (zoom) with Staff from SANDAG re their Vision Zero Program. This program is still a work in progress and they estimate that it won’t be completed for at least the next few months.
Vision Zero
sandag.org

Vision Zero is a comprehensive data driven program to identify roads/areas in our region that have the highest concentration of major accidents where law enforcement has been involved and reports have been generated.

With this accident information, these areas have then been analyzed to determine what changes or improvements could be made so that there could potentially be zero future accidents.

This information could then also be used by municipalities and the County to apply for approximately $1 billion dollars in federal grants.

One of the concerns that I have is that this data is 2 years behind, so the numbers are from 2022. It seems to me that after Covid, the public generally appears to be driving a lot faster and in a much more unsafe manner, hence an increase in accidents that these initial studies might not capture.

Below is a link for the SANDAG’s interactive map associated with this program. It shows the areas that have the highest concentration of accidents, amongst other data.
Traffic Safety Dashboard
opendata.sandag.org

While SANDAG’s goal for this program is to provide the data to help with grants, I see this as a great tool to use when we are asking DPW and TAC to reduce speeds and study roads in our area for traffic calming or other ways to reduce accidents.

A few of you asked at the last meeting whether your planning group can send a letter to SANDAG on this. I asked County Counsel and pasted their response below. It is marked privileged so please keep it to the chairs and do not post or forward it.

PRIVILEGED AND CONFIDENTIAL – ATTORNEY-CLIENT COMMUNICATION
Eileen – Planning groups are advisory to the Board of Supervisors and PDS under Board Policy I-1. A group can send comments to SANDAG, but only as an action of the group, voted on at a noticed meeting with the item on the agenda, and the letter should say it is the group’s recommendation. A chair cannot send a letter on behalf of the group without that vote. Individual members can comment as residents but need to make clear they are not speaking for their group.
Marcus Hollis, Deputy County Counsel

I’ll keep you posted when I get further updates. If you have any questions, please let me know.
Best regards,

Eileen Delaney
Vice Chair, APG- San Diego County

Eileen Delaney, Chair
Fallbrook Planning Group
Fallbrook Design Review Board
Follow The FPG on Facebook
Fallbrook Planning Group | Facebook

Visit our website for current meeting information
Fallbrook Planning Group – Serving Our Community

Date: Tue, May 27, 2025 at 4:12 PM
Subject: RE: [External] Zoom for Thursday meeting
To: Travis Lyon <travislyonacpg@gmail.com>


PRIVILEGED AND CONFIDENTIAL
ATTORNEY-CLIENT COMMUNICATION

Travis,

Short answer is no. Members who join by Zoom only count toward the quorum if the Brown Act teleconference requirements are met, and for Thursday they won't be.

Under the traditional rules (Gov. Code 54953(b)(3)) each remote member's location has to be listed on the posted agenda, the agenda has to be posted at that location, and the location has to be open to the public. Your agenda for Thursday is already posted and doesn't list any remote locations, so that option is out for this meeting.

The AB 2449 option (54953(f)) requires a quorum to be physically present at the meeting location to begin with, so it won't help you get to a quorum. It is also limited to "just cause" (childcare or caregiving, contagious illness, a disability-related need, or travel on official business) or emergency circumstances, the member has to be on camera the whole time, and they have to disclose if anyone 18 or older is in the room with them. Just cause can only be used twice per calendar year.

So you need a quorum in the room. If you don't have one, the members present can adjourn but can't take any other action. Members of the public can still watch and comment by Zoom.

Let me know if you have any other questions.

Adrienne

body:
PRIVILEGED & CONFIDENTIAL – ATTORNEY-CLIENT COMMUNICATION

Hi Travis,

Yes, you can forward the notice to the members and post it on the Facebook page. Sending informational material out one-way is fine. What you want to avoid is members replying all with their views on the NOFA criteria. A majority of members exchanging views by email on something that could come before the group is a serial meeting under Gov. Code 54952.2(b), even if nobody intends it that way. I'd add a line at the top of your forward asking members not to reply all.

On comments, the ACPG can only submit comments as the group after it discusses and votes on them at a noticed meeting. Since June 27 is after the June 10 deadline, your options are (1) call a special meeting with at least 24 hours notice under 54956, or (2) members submit comments individually as residents. If they go individually, they should not describe their comments as the ACPG's position or sign as ACPG members in a way that suggests the group has acted.

Happy to walk through the special meeting notice if you want to go that route.

Adrienne

Hi Travis,

The County of San Diego's Land Use & Environment Group (LUEG) is conducting a series of public meetings from May 20 - June 4 to gather public feedback and input on an upcoming Notice of Funding Availability (NOFA) on a $9 million ARPA-funded grant program to help address broadband access and affordability in unincorporated communities. body:
PRIVILEGED AND CONFIDENTIAL
ATTORNEY-CLIENT COMMUNICATION / ATTORNEY WORK PRODUCT

Travis,

Answers to your questions below.

1. April 4 meeting. Since it isn't your regular meeting date it is a special meeting under Gov. Code 54956. The agenda/notice has to be delivered to each member and posted at least 24 hours before the meeting, and the group can only take up the items listed on it. If you post in the same place you post your regular agendas you should be fine.

2. Applicant not attending. There is no requirement that the applicant be present for the group to make a recommendation. That said, the applicant has indicated the design is being revised in response to County comments, so the group may want to continue the item to April 25 rather than make a recommendation on a design that is going to change. Either way, the ACPG's recommendation is advisory and PDS will keep processing the application within the federal and state timeframes that apply to wireless facilities. The group's schedule does not extend those deadlines.

3. Health concerns. Under federal law (47 U.S.C. 332(c)(7)(B)(iv)) the County cannot deny or condition a wireless facility on the basis of the environmental effects of RF emissions if the facility complies with the FCC's emission standards. Residents can still raise it in public comment, but the group should not base its recommendation on RF health effects. A recommendation based on aesthetics, siting, height, and consistency with the Alpine Community Plan is appropriate.

Hani - please let me know if the revised plans come in before the 25th.

Adrienne

subject: RE: [External] Fwd: Maggie/ Greg SDGE Loveland Progress!
body:
PRIVILEGED & CONFIDENTIAL – ATTORNEY-CLIENT COMMUNICATION

Travis,

There's no prohibition on members belonging to or attending meetings of a community organization like Friends of Loveland Reservoir, and being copied on emails from members of the public is not by itself a Brown Act issue.

The concern is serial communications. If a majority of ACPG members end up on the same email chain or at the same Friends meeting and discuss or share their views with each other on Loveland issues that are likely to come before the ACPG, that can be a serial meeting under Gov. Code 54952.2(b), including when it happens through a third party passing views along. The exception in 54952.2(c)(3) for attending a community meeting organized by another group only applies as long as the members don't discuss ACPG business among themselves outside the scheduled program.

So my recommendations: don't reply all on these chains, don't share your views on Loveland with other members outside of a noticed meeting, and if it is going to be on an ACPG agenda, save the discussion for the meeting.

Adrienne

body:
PRIVILEGED AND CONFIDENTIAL – ATTORNEY-CLIENT COMMUNICATION

Hi Travis,

Yes, you can do the interview. Since the group hasn't discussed or taken a position on the feasibility study or consolidation with Padre Dam, you should make clear at the start that you are speaking as an individual member and not for the ACPG. You can describe actions the group has taken in the past on water issues if they are reflected in approved minutes.

If the Study team wants the ACPG's position, the item would need to go on an agenda for discussion and a vote at a noticed meeting. The group could also invite the Study team to present at a meeting, which would let the other members and the public weigh in.

Please don't poll the other members by email on what to say in the interview.

Adrienne

Good afternoon,

My name is Marissa, with Katz & Associates, and I'm part of a team under the California State Water Resources Control Board that is studying the feasibility of consolidating properties with individual groundwater wells or independent water systems east of Alpine with the Padre Dam Municipal Water District.

I'm reaching out today to see if you're interested in participating in an interview that will inform a Feasibility Study.

Background
The California State Water Resources Control Board<https://www.waterboards.ca.gov/> (Board) under the Safe and Affordable Funding for Equity and Resilience (Safer) Drinking Water Program<https://www.waterboards.ca.gov/water_issues/programs/grants_loans/sustainable_water_solutions/safer.html>, is funding planning efforts, including a Feasibility Study (Study), to support communities and help ensure a safe and reliable water supply for the future.

Due to some water quality concerns of existing groundwater wells in the Willowside Terrace community, located just east of the city of Alpine, the Board is conducting a Study to determine if this community can be connected to the Padre Dam Municipal Water District<https://www.padredam.org/> (PDMWD) to ensure a high quality, reliable and sustainable water supply is available for the future.

The Study team is interested in forming an expanded study area to include additional properties near Willowside Terrace that also use an independent water system reliant on groundwater.

As the Alpine Community Planning Group, the Study team is interested in participating in an interview with you to gather insights into the communities east of Alpine, near the potential study area. The Study team is interested in a range of views, opinions and experiences about independent water systems, the services provided by PDMWD, and the possibility of consolidating independent water systems with the district

Please let me know if you are interested in participating in an interview and what your availability looks like for the next few weeks.

I look forward to hearing from you.

body:
PRIVILEGED & CONFIDENTIAL
ATTORNEY-CLIENT COMMUNICATION

Travis,

Yes. Emails that relate to the conduct of ACPG business can be public records under the Public Records Act even when they are sent or received on a personal account. (City of San Jose v. Superior Court (2017) 2 Cal.5th 608.) That includes notices like this one from SDG&E, emails with applicants and County staff, and emails between members about ACPG matters. Purely personal emails are not.

Please don't delete ACPG-related emails. If the County receives a PRA request for ACPG records, PDS will ask members to search their accounts and provide anything responsive, and we will review for exemptions before anything is released. It helps to use a dedicated account for ACPG business, like the one you are using now, and to encourage the other members to do the same or at least keep ACPG emails in a separate folder or label.

Please don't forward this email, it is privileged.

Adrienne

PRIVILEGED AND CONFIDENTIAL – ATTORNEY-CLIENT COMMUNICATION

Travis,

If Mr. Walsh meets with fewer than a majority of the members, that is not a meeting under the Brown Act. If a majority of members meet with him together, or if he meets with members one after another and passes along what each of them said to the others, it becomes a meeting (or serial meeting) under Gov. Code 54952.2 and would have to be noticed and open to the public.

If he wants the whole group to see his documents, the better approach is to agendize a presentation at a regular meeting. That keeps it public and gives other members of the public a chance to comment.

On the trail grant rubric, the ACPG doesn't have a role in selecting projects for Senator Jones's office or the grant unless the group votes to send a recommendation. Individual members should be careful not to represent that the ACPG supports any particular project or rubric.

subject: RE: Objective Design Standards (ODS) Checklist - Alpine
body:
Good morning,

Thank you for your continued coordination with our Objective Design Standards (ODS) project. As discussed, State laws that are already in effect require that any housing developments eligible for streamlining approval be reviewed with clear, objective standards regarding design aspects such as materials, colors, etc. Typically, these would be projects that include affordable housing units.  Design standards that are not objective cannot be applied to these projects.

To ensure we have objective design standards available for any potential applications, our team used your existing Design Review Checklist as a template to create an Objective Design Review Checklist that clarifies any subjective language and maintains the visual integrity of housing developments in your community. We kindly request your group send any feedback on the checklist by August 15th, 2024.

The Objective Design Review Checklist will serve as a supplemental form for projects eligible for streamlined approval under state law. It will not replace the current Design Review Checklist<https://www.sandiegocounty.gov/content/dam/sdc/pds/drb/AlpineDesignReviewChecklistFINAL1.pdf>, which will continue to apply to projects not eligible for the streamlined review. While no applications for this streamlined process have been submitted in your Community Planning Area, the Objective Design Review Checklist will be applicable if one is received. We are finalizing this Objective Design Review Checklist and will make it easily accessible online for potential applications eligible for these State laws.

Attached is the draft Objective Design Review version of your community’s existing Design Review Checklist, and a map delineating potentially eligible areas for this streamlined process. A strikethrough indicates a proposed removal of language, while an underline indicates a proposed change/addition.  Also attached is a PDF version for your reference. There may also be highlighted language or comment bubbles that we are requesting specific feedback on, regarding unclear language or unclear measurements.  There are additional details in the original e-mail below.

Please keep in mind this is still a working draft. It has not been through County Counsel or management review yet, and some of the proposed language (particularly the building step-back and roofline articulation measurements) is still being discussed internally, so we left the alternative options in the comment bubbles rather than selecting one. We ask that the group not post or circulate the draft outside of the members until the final version is released.

We will work to incorporate your suggestions into the checklist which will be accessible on our website in Fall 2024. While there is some flexibility to make changes in the future, staff availability and allocation may make it challenging to respond urgently to suggestions for edits after that date. Therefore, please ensure you submit any requests for modifications by August 15th, 2024, so your feedback can be incorporated into the checklist before it is made available online.

Please let us know if you have any questions as you review the document. We appreciate your continued collaboration and commitment to enhancing our unincorporated communities.

[cid:image001.png@01DA7ABA.EF015A80]<http://www.sdcpds.org/>
Luis Duran
Planner III | Planning & Development Services | Long Range Planning
County of San Diego | 5510 Overland Ave. Suite 310 | San Diego, CA 92123|
• (619) 214-4698  |  • Luis.Duran@sdcounty.ca.gov<mailto:Luis.Duran@sdcounty.ca.gov>

From: Duran, Luis
Sent: Friday, March 22, 2024 4:03 PM
To: travislyonacpg@gmail.com
Subject: Objective Design Standards (ODS) Checklist - Alpine

Hello Chair Lyon,

I hope this email finds you well. Following our recent presentation at your Community Planning Group (CPG) meeting on February 22, 2024. I am pleased to update you on the latest progress regarding the Objective Design Standards (ODS) project.

To recap, our presentation centered around State laws which allow for a streamlined process for eligible multifamily projects, and how design standards can be implemented in that process. Eligible projects need to meet all eligibility requirements and objective design standards at the time of application, or their development cannot be streamlined through a ministerial process. Our project team is working to edit your existing Design Review Checklist to clarify any subjective language to maintain the visual integrity of your community in the case an eligible project application is submitted. Attached is a draft “Objective” version of the Alpine Checklist with a corresponding map, delineating potentially eligible areas for streamlined housing development.

A few notes as you review the attached documents:

MAP: State law states that a multifamily development “contains two or more residential units”.  According to the California Department of Housing and Community Development, a new single-family development and an attached accessory dwelling unit when built together are considered multifamily and are eligible for streamlining under SB 35.  An applicant would still need to meet all eligibility requirements to streamline their project. These eligible parcels are distinguished by a pink color.  The blue parcels are eligible for streamlining under State law, where three or more units can be built under current Zoning. The attached maps have been updated to reflect recent State laws in effect as of March 2024.

CHECKLIST: Attached is a Microsoft Word document containing tracked changes.  A strikethrough indicates a proposed removal of language, while an underline indicates proposed change/addition.  Also attached is a PDF version for your reference. The Design Review Checklist for your community may include goals or intentions related to your original Design Guidelines. As this draft is for ease of use, we have removed these to strictly focus on the design standards that must be followed. This makes the checklist shorter and easier to read. There may also be highlighted language or comment bubbles that we are requesting specific feedback on, regarding unclear language or unclear measurements.

As discussed previously, this project will not be updating or changing Alpine’s Form Based Code (FBC).  The Draft Objective Design Standards Checklist attached is for the areas not covered by the FBC.  We kindly request your group review the attached Checklist to ensure that it accurately reflects the intent of your existing community’s design standards. Please submit your initial feedback no later than April 23rd, 2024.

We appreciate your collaboration and commitment to enhancing our unincorporated communities.

For further information on ODS, please visit the following links: Objective Design Standards | Engage San Diego County<https://engage.sandiegocounty.gov/ods> and Objective Design Standards (sandiegocounty.gov)<https://www.sandiegocounty.gov/content/sdc/pds/longrangeplanning/ods/>

subject: DRAFT - Park Fee Changes Starting February 18, 2025
body:
Hi Travis,

Before this goes out to the public next week I wanted to give you a preview of the draft notice, since the Alpine folks will be asking you about it at your meetings. This is still a working draft and hasn't been through our Director's office or Communications yet, so please don't forward it or post it. The items in brackets are still being discussed internally and could change. If you have thoughts on how it will land in Alpine I'd appreciate hearing them by Friday.

----- DRAFT - NOT FOR DISTRIBUTION -----

At the County of San Diego Parks and Recreation Department, we take great pride in maintaining beautiful, safe, and accessible outdoor spaces for everyone to enjoy. To continue providing high-quality parks, trails, and recreation services, we will be making some adjustments to our park service fees starting February 18, 2025.
This is our first fee update in nearly 11 years, and while we’ve worked hard to keep costs as low as possible, this change is necessary to help offset rising maintenance and operating expenses. The updates also align our fees with similar parks and facilities in the region while ensuring that we continue to deliver best-in-nation outdoor experiences. [Deputy Director asked if we keep "best-in-nation" - open]

What’s Changing?
Most of the fee increases are just a few dollars, but they will help us keep our parks safe, clean, and well-maintained for generations to come. Here are a few examples of the adjustments:

  *   Day Use Parking: Increasing from $3.00 to $5.00 per day
  *   RV Partial Hook-Up Campsite: Increasing from $29 to $35 per night
  *   Camping Reservations: Now include up to two pets and one extra vehicle at no additional cost [pending sign-off, may move to separate notice]
  *   Other small increases apply to rentals, permits, and additional park services

To see the full list of updated fees, please visit our 2025_DPR_User_Fee_Changes_01.17.25.pdf<https://www.sdparks.org/content/dam/sdparks/en/pdf/public-meetings/fee_increase/2025_DPR_User_Fee_Changes_01.17.25.pdf>. For more information on why these changes are happening, check out our FAQs_Park User Fee Increase 01.17.25.pdf<https://www.sdparks.org/content/dam/sdparks/en/pdf/public-meetings/fee_increase/FAQs_Park%20User%20Fee%20Increase%2001.17.25.pdf>.

Why Are Fees Increasing?
The cost of maintaining our 158 parks, 389 miles of trails, and over 58,000 acres of land has risen significantly over the past decade. Adjusting our fees will allow us to:
✔ Continue offering high-quality park experiences and amenities
✔ Keep trails, facilities, and green spaces safe and well-maintained
✔ Expand and improve park programs and services for all ages and abilities
[Still deciding whether to add a line on the day use lots in the Alpine/East County area - Carl]
Even with these updates, our park fees remain affordable and continue to offer exceptional value compared to similar park systems.

Ensuring Parks Remain Accessible for Everyone
We believe that everyone should have access to nature—which is why we continue to offer financial assistance programs and free or low-cost activities:
🌿 Discounted Programs: Veterans, seniors, and groups may qualify for discounts on fees and reservations.
🏕 First-Time Camping Program: A free initiative designed to introduce new campers to the joys of the outdoors.
🎉 Low-Cost or Free Activities: Most of our recreation programs and events are available at reduced or no cost.
We are committed to making the outdoors accessible and enjoyable for all members of our community.

Thank You for Your Support!
We appreciate your understanding and continued support as we make these necessary updates. Your visits, participation, and enthusiasm help keep our parks vibrant and welcoming for everyone.
If you have any questions or would like more details, please visit our Fees Increase Feb. 18<https://www.sdparks.org/content/sdparks/en/news-events/news-stories/Fees-Increase-Feb-18.html>.

We look forward to seeing you at the parks!
